newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: World Bank urges Colombia restrain spending - report.
newsitem.headline: World Bank urges Colombia restrain spending - report.

text.p: Colombia must not increase public spending in a bid to pull the country out of its first recession in decades, World Bank senior economist for Latin America Guillermo Perry said Monday.

In an interview with the leading El Tiempo newspaper, Perry said the World Bank was certain that the Colombian economy had solid fundamentals and that recovery could be achieved with careful medium-term management.

Perry, former Colombian finance minister in President Ernesto Samper's administration, declined to say when he thought the economy would return to positive growth but said domestic and foreign investment and exports would spearhead the recovery. "Increasing public spending would create more problems and the government knows that and has been austere in its spending plans," Perry said.
"Driving up public spending in an open economy doesn't work. If spending rises quickly but revenue doesn't increase at the same speed then this will generate a greater deficit," he added.

Last week, the government's National Planning Department said the gross domestic product posted negative growth of 1.22 percent in the first quarter of this year, following negative growth of 0.1 percent in the last quarter of 1996.
It is the first time in at least 50 years that Colombia, traditionally a country of sustained economic growth, has been plunged into recession.
But Perry was upbeat about future prospects for Colombia's economy.
"The World Bank, multilateral organizations and the financial system see solid fundamentals in the Colombian economy and are convinced in (the government's) good economic management," he said.

"If Colombia avoids a revaluation of the peso currency, if interest rates fall and if the government fosters a climate of investor confidence, then the country should return to reasonable growth," he added.

Perry urged the government and Congress to tackle structural problems in public spending and rein back the yawning fiscal deficit. Last year the central government deficit was running in excess of four percent of gross domestic product.
The senior World Bank economist said Colombia should observe solutions applied in Argentina and Mexico to overcome their economic slumps -- boosting private sector investment and promoting exports.
